questions.q: 'Donor dominance' (Orentreich, 1959) — the principle underlying all hair transplantation — means:
opts: The recipient site re-programmes transplanted follicles to local characteristics
DHT-sensitive follicles become DHT-resistant after transplantation due to improved vascularity
Donor zone hair density always exceeds recipient zone density genetically
Transplanted follicles retain the genetic DHT-resistance of the donor zone regardless of the new scalp environment
questions.exp:
Orentreich's donor dominance (1959): follicles harvested from the permanent occipital/parietal zone (DHT-resistant) continue to behave genetically as they did at the donor site — they do NOT miniaturise at the DHT-rich vertex. This is the biological rationale for hair transplantation.
🏰 Palace: DONOR FOLLICLES are FOREIGN AMBASSADORS carrying their OWN COUNTRY'S PASSPORT (DHT-resistant genes) — they refuse to obey the RECIPIENT SCALP'S DHT laws, growing forever in their new territory.

questions.q: The 'safe donor zone' in androgenetic alopecia is located:
opts: Any scalp area with visible hair regardless of AGA progression
The temporal region bilaterally only
Permanent occipital and parietal scalp bounded by the Mayer-Paul line — DHT-resistant follicles
The entire posterior scalp below the external occipital protuberance
questions.exp:
The safe donor zone (SDZ) is the permanent fringe of hair at the posterior and lateral scalp, bounded superiorly by the Mayer-Paul line. These follicles are genetically programmed to resist DHT-driven miniaturisation. Harvesting outside this zone risks using impermanent follicles that will eventually miniaturise.
🏰 Palace: SAFE DONOR ZONE = the PERMANENT FRINGE CASTLE — the MAYER-PAUL LINE is its northern wall; follicles inside survive forever, those outside eventually surrender to DHT.

questions.q: Follicular unit transplantation (FUT) differs from FUE in that:
opts: FUT uses smaller (0.7mm) punches than FUE
FUT harvests a strip of scalp under direct vision (lower transection rate, higher single-session yield) leaving a linear scar; FUE extracts individual units leaving only punctate scars
FUT avoids all scarring, unlike FUE which leaves a linear scar
FUT is preferred for beard-hair transplantation
questions.exp:
FUT (strip harvest): excise 1–2cm wide strip → stereomicroscope dissection of FUs → 3000–6000+ grafts/session, transection <5%, linear scar. FUE: 0.7–1.2mm punch extraction of individual FUs → punctate scars (<1mm), no linear scar, slower, higher transection 5–20%, lower graft yield per session.
🏰 Palace: FUT = STRIP MINING (one linear trench, low transection, thousands of gems); FUE = INDIVIDUAL COIN-DIGGING (no scar, slower, chip more gems per dig).

questions.q: In FUE, which punch type produces the LOWEST follicular transection rate?
opts: Blunt Harris punch used with oscillation
Motorised drill punch at maximum RPM
Serrated punch for fibrotic donor areas
Sharp-edged trumpet/trumpet punch used with controlled rotation depth
questions.exp:
Punch types: sharp (low transection, ideal for straight fine hair), blunt (Harris punch for coily/curly hair where follicle angle changes mid-dermis), serrated (for fibrotic scalp). Robotic FUE (ARTAS) uses image-guided sharp punch reducing transection to <5%. Transection rate is the key quality metric in FUE.
🏰 Palace: SHARP TRUMPET PUNCH is the PRECISION SURGEON — quick clean cut around the follicle; BLUNT HARRIS is the RUGBY PLAYER — pushes through curly-hair curves without slicing.

questions.q: DUPA (Diffuse Unpatterned Alopecia) is a contraindication to hair transplantation because:
opts: Miniaturisation affects the 'safe donor zone' too, so transplanted follicles will also eventually miniaturise
These patients have insufficient scalp laxity for FUT strip harvesting
DUPA patients cannot tolerate local anaesthesia
The recipient area has too much fibrosis for graft placement
questions.exp:
In DUPA, the miniaturisation process does not follow the typical AGA pattern and invades the 'permanent' occipital zone. Trichoscopy reveals miniaturised hairs throughout the safe donor zone. Transplanting these follicles guarantees eventual miniaturisation and loss of transplanted hair. DUPA must be excluded before surgery by careful trichoscopic donor zone assessment.
🏰 Palace: DUPA = the SAFE DONOR ZONE HAS BEEN INVADED — miniaturised follicles are TRAITORS wearing DHT-resistant DISGUISE; transplant them and they eventually MINIATURISE in the new castle too.

questions.q: The maximum recommended 'out-of-body' time for follicular unit grafts to maintain viability above 90% is:
opts: 4–6 hours in chilled (4°C) normal saline or Ringer's lactate
30 minutes at room temperature
12 hours in warmed (37°C) saline
24 hours in HypoThermosol FRS at room temperature
questions.exp:
Grafts must be kept in chilled isotonic solution (4°C saline, Ringer's lactate, or ATP-supplemented solutions). At 4°C, metabolic demand drops and ischaemic tolerance extends to 4–6 hours. Beyond 6h, viability falls. Room temperature accelerates necrosis. Grafts must never dry out — they should remain fully submerged.
🏰 Palace: GRAFTS in a 4°C ICE BOX survive 4–6 HOURS like orchids in a chilled delivery van — take them out of the ice and they WILT within the hour.

questions.q: The DHI (Direct Hair Implantation) technique uses the Choi implanter pen. Its key advantage over conventional slit-and-place FUE is:
opts: Larger grafts (3–4 FU) can be placed with higher density
DHI allows deeper graft placement reaching the subcutaneous fat
Simultaneous channel creation and graft implantation reduces graft out-of-body exposure time and desiccation
DHI does not require any recipient site shaving
questions.exp:
Choi pen: a hollow needle (0.6–1.5mm diameter) into which the graft is loaded; the pen simultaneously penetrates the scalp and deposits the graft — no pre-made slits required. Benefits: minimal graft handling, shorter desiccation time, precise angle/depth control. Higher implanter cost and slower process than pre-made slits.
🏰 Palace: CHOI PEN = a SYRINGE + PLANTER IN ONE — load the graft, stab the scalp, push the plunger — no pre-cut slit needed, graft goes directly from cold storage into the crown castle.

questions.q: The standard hairline design for a male with Norwood III vertex pattern should place the midpoint of the anterior hairline at approximately:
opts: 7–9 cm above the nasion (glabellar midpoint), with appropriate temporal recession
Exactly at the same level as the patient's original adolescent hairline
5 cm above nasion — the classic female hairline height
10–12 cm above nasion for a mature male appearance
questions.exp:
Male hairline design: 7–9 cm above the nasion at the midpoint (average 8–8.5 cm in adult males). Positioning too low creates a feminised or adolescent look; too high looks unnatural. Temporal recession (widow's peak) must be respected. The hairline should be irregular (irregular, not a straight line) with single-follicle units at the front.
🏰 Palace: MALE HAIRLINE at 7–9 cm above the NOSE CASTLE BRIDGE — 5cm is FEMININE, 10–12cm is MONK-BALD; the GOLDILOCKS zone is 7–9 cm.

questions.q: Shock loss (effluvium) after hair transplantation refers to:
opts: Scarring alopecia at FUT donor site linear scar
Temporary shedding of pre-existing native hair near graft sites due to operative trauma, usually reversible within 3–4 months
Permanent loss of all transplanted grafts due to poor vascularisation
Post-operative folliculitis causing permanent hair loss
questions.exp:
Shock loss (traumatic effluvium): miniaturised or telogen-prone native hairs adjacent to graft sites shed transiently due to physical trauma (anaesthetic infiltration, needle passes, oedema). Usually reversible within 3–6 months as follicles re-enter anagen. More common in thinning areas with advanced miniaturisation. Cannot occur in areas of complete baldness.
🏰 Palace: SHOCK LOSS = the native hair SOLDIERS faint from trauma (anaesthesia, needle trauma) and go AWOL (shed) temporarily — most return from LEAVE in 3–4 months.

questions.q: When using platelet-rich plasma (PRP) adjuvant during hair transplantation, it is most typically applied at which stage?
opts: Taken orally as pre-operative supplementation
Injected into the donor site after strip excision only
Injected into recipient sites or used as graft storage medium — to improve graft survival and wound healing
Applied topically to the scalp pre-operatively only
questions.exp:
Intraoperative PRP use in HT: (1) grafts soaked in PRP solution during storage; (2) injected into recipient sites before/after graft placement; (3) injected into donor wound for healing. Growth factors (PDGF, VEGF, TGF-β) improve graft survival, accelerate healing, and may reduce shock loss. Evidence level is moderate but growing.
🏰 Palace: PRP is the PLATELET FERTILISER BATH soaking grafts in GROWTH FACTOR SOUP — the transplanted seeds get a HEAD START in the new castle soil.

questions.q: Body hair transplantation (BHT) using beard or chest hair as donor source has which limitation compared to scalp FUE?
opts: Beard hair must be transplanted only to the beard area due to anatomical programming
Body hair grafts always produce permanent results identical to scalp hair
Body hair FUE is faster than scalp FUE and has lower transection rates
Body/beard hairs have shorter anagen cycles, smaller calibre, and curved follicles → lower yield and different texture at recipient site
questions.exp:
Body/beard hair as donor: shorter anagen (1–2y vs 3–6y scalp = shorter terminal hair), different calibre (beard often coarser), curved follicles (higher transection), single-follicle units (not 2–4 FU like scalp). Used when scalp donor exhausted. Beard hair for scalp gives reasonable density; chest/back hair gives short, fine cover. Match texture expectations carefully.
🏰 Palace: BODY HAIR is the BACKUP DONOR from foreign provinces — shorter anagen PASSPORT (only 1–2 year reign), curvy FOLLICLE PATH (harder to extract), different TEXTURE than the native scalp hair.

questions.q: The Norwood-Hamilton scale for male AGA has how many stages and what pattern defines Stage VI?
opts: 7 stages; Stage VI = isolated mid-scalp island of hair
10 stages; Stage VI is moderate vertex involvement
7 stages; Stage VI = large bald area joining bitemporal recession and vertex, only a horseshoe fringe remains
5 stages; Stage VI is the most severe with complete baldness
questions.exp:
Norwood-Hamilton: 7 stages (I–VII). Stage VI = advanced balding with the bald area at front/top connecting to the crown; only a permanent horseshoe fringe of hair remains. Stage VII = most severe, the fringe is very narrow. Planning a transplant at Stage VI requires accepting limited density across a large area.
🏰 Palace: NORWOOD 7-FLOOR CASTLE: by FLOOR VI the ROOF IS NEARLY GONE — only the HORSESHOE FRINGE CASTLE WALL stands around the sides; by FLOOR VII even that's thin.

questions.q: For the ideal FUE graft, the harvested follicular unit should include which anatomical components?
opts: Hair shaft + follicle bulb + dermal papilla + peribulbar connective tissue + a small ring of epidermis (the bulge region for stem cells)
Dermis and hypodermis with no bulge region needed
The arrector pili muscle must be included for survival
Hair shaft and cortex only
questions.exp:
A complete, viable FU graft includes: the hair shaft(s), the infundibulum (upper follicle), the isthmus containing the bulge region (hair follicle stem cells — critical for regeneration), the follicle bulb and matrix cells, and the dermal papilla. The peribulbar fat (adipose cushion) should be preserved. The arrector pili is not critical.
🏰 Palace: PERFECT GRAFT = HAIR SHAFT + BULGE STEM CELL KEEP + DERMAL PAPILLA THRONE at the base — lose the BULGE and the stem cells are gone; lose the PAPILLA and no new hair is possible.

questions.q: Trichophytic closure of the FUT donor strip wound helps conceal the scar by:
opts: Bevelling one wound edge so hair follicles grow through the scar, camouflaging the linear mark
Applying fibrin glue to eliminate any visible line
Laser resurfacing of the donor scar immediately at wound closure
Using absorbable sutures that dissolve without leaving a line
questions.exp:
Trichophytic closure: the superior (or inferior) wound edge is bevelled/trimmed by 2–3mm to expose follicle tips, then the edges are closed so follicular stumps at the trimmed margin grow up through the scar. Hairs emerging through the scar visually disguise the linear line. Requires good tension-free closure and multi-layer (galea + skin) suturing.
🏰 Palace: TRICHOPHYTIC CLOSURE = GRASS GROWING THROUGH the CASTLE WALL CRACK — by bevelling the wound edge, HAIR SPROUTS through the scar itself, making it INVISIBLE from above.

questions.q: A 32-year-old with Norwood III vertex asks about hair transplant planning. Which assessment is MOST CRITICAL before designing the transplant?
opts: Patch test with local anaesthetic 48 hours pre-operatively
Trichoscopic assessment of donor zone miniaturisation to confirm follicles are truly permanent and rule out DUPA
Blood group typing for potential allogenic graft compatibility
Hormone assay to check DHT levels on the day of surgery
questions.exp:
Pre-HT trichoscopy is critical: (1) assess donor zone miniaturisation ratio — if >20% miniaturised hairs in the safe donor zone, the patient may have DUPA or diffuse AGA extending into the permanent zone, making transplant inadvisable; (2) assess recipient zone density to plan graft count; (3) identify hair calibre, angle, direction for harvesting. DHT levels do not guide surgical planning.
🏰 Palace: TRICHOSCOPY is the PRE-BATTLE INTELLIGENCE REPORT — before transplanting ONE SOLDIER, check if the SAFE DONOR BARRACKS is infiltrated by MINIATURISED TRAITORS (>20% = DUPA risk = abort mission).
